name: zaro-video
$comment: x264 and x265 are external libraries behind feature flags, and this build
asks for them because the code asks for them by name: MakeProxy.cpp
encodes proxies with libx264, Encoder.cpp defaults to it for anything
that is not a .mov, and the Deliver panel offers an HEVC preset that
names libx265. Without these features avcodec_find_encoder_by_name
returns null on Windows alone, and the proxy and render paths fail
there while passing everywhere else -- macOS and Linux take FFmpeg
from Homebrew and the distribution, and both ship it with x264 built
in. The gpl feature is what x264 and x265 require; naming it here
makes the licence of the Windows binary a stated choice rather than a
side effect, and it matches what the other two platforms already link.
Consumed only when the build is configured with vcpkg's toolchain file,
which is what the windows-* presets do. macOS and Linux keep resolving
these through Homebrew and the distribution respectively, so this manifest
is inert there.
Qt is deliberately absent: building qtbase from source costs hours, so CI
and developers both take it from the official binaries (aqt / Homebrew /
the distribution) and point CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH at it.
Catch2 is absent for a different reason: the top-level CMakeLists fetches
and builds it in-tree on every platform, because a prebuilt one is built
to C++14 and will not link against our C++20 test sources.
pkgconf is a host dependency because cmake/FindFFmpeg.cmake locates FFmpeg
through pkg-config, which Windows has no system copy of.
